coordinates.origin: Whole fish centered, meters, up+Z; no slab or pedestal

concept.reason: Actual full fossil with labeled fins and scale, published specimen figure, and upper/lower tooth plate photographs are available; no generated concept needed.

extra_views.reason: Targeted diagnostic after early mouth inspection found throat backing obscuring radial tooth-plate ridges. The repaired exact GLB closeup shows paired low radiating plates, not fangs.

scope: Original 609 whole living lungfish. Two clearly separate dorsal fins and blunt tooth-plate-bearing head. No slab, detached jaw, or fin-only substitution.
reference_specimen: BMNH P22187, Charest et al 2023 Fig 9; Achanarras complete fossil IMG_6882a as additional body/scale reference

scale.status: Approximate specimen-informed artistic scale: Achanarras IMG_6882a has 2 cm bar about110px versus fish about1100px (~20cm); not a published precise measurement. PLOS Fig9 has10mm bar.
scale.uncertainty: Body thickness and living soft tissues reconstructed, not measured from compressed specimen; do not describe20cm as species maximum.

material_policy: Restrained slate olive dorsal body, muted lighter belly, dark eyes and pale tooth plates. Colors speculative; opaque flat palette, no fossil photos as texture.
diagnostic_targets: Compact robust elongated fish body with broad blunt rounded snout, small eyes and opercular boundary.
Two discrete dorsal fins: smaller first near rear half and larger second posteriorly, with a visible bare-backed gap. Do not fuse into modern lungfish continuous median fin.
Paired fleshy-based pectoral fins and paired pelvic fins farther posterior; pointed leaf-like anal fin below posterior dorsal.
Second dorsal longer/higher than anal, verified Charest2023; separate asymmetrical caudal fin, following labeled fossil outline rather than shark deeply forked tail.
Slightly open mouth must reveal paired lower tooth plates with low radiating cusped ridges, and opposed upper plates if visible. No large conical fangs or marginal shark tooth row.
Simplified scale fields and fin rays are subordinate to silhouette. Real three-dimensional volume and fin roots; not a textured plane.
uncertainties: Living body cross-section, skin color and soft lip margins speculative.
Source fossils are laterally compressed, dorsal/ventral fin overlap can conceal paired fins. Use bilateral paired fins, not all fins on one side.
Tooth plate cusp count is simplified, not exact histological reconstruction; tiny structures may be proportionally clarified without detached oversized props.
acceptance_checklist: Whole living animal and original diagnostic pair retained.
Side view shows distinct dorsal fins and gap, separate anal and tail; second dorsal larger than anal.
Front/perspective reveals blunt head and tooth plates, not hidden closed mouth or tusks.
Paired pectoral and pelvic fins connect anatomically without isolated floating roots.
Four standard exact-GLB views; self-contained source, two rebuilds, independent QA.
